How does encapsulation work in Python? What is name mangling?

Supplied answer
A single underscore (_name) is a convention meaning "internal, please do not touch". A double
underscore (__name) triggers name mangling: Python renames it to _ClassName__name so it cannot
be accessed accidentally from outside or by a subclass. It is protection by convention, not real security -
the mangled name is still reachable.
